responses.text: Wording only, no item digest changed (gate 3031db2a50b0a036 again). AttnFwd.lean's module docstring now gives the test as test_op, lines 631-695, and the benchmark as lines 698-780 (its configs, bench_flash_attention at 739-775, and its run), as the source has them; README's benchmark range (was 706-775) is corrected the same way. I also checked every other source line reference in the folder against source/: two proof-module docstrings and one comment cited line 87 for acc * alpha[:, None], which is line 95 (RowAcc.scale_err, Step's module docstring and astep), now corrected.

Wording only, no item digest changed. README (Specification) and HeadOk's docstring now give one figure with its argument: sm_scale*sum_e|q_e k_e| = sm_scale*s^2*sum_e|X_e Y_e| with X, Y independent standard normals (test s = 0.5, sm_scale = 0.5; benchmark s = 1, sm_scale = 1.3); its mean at D = 128 is about 10 (test) and 106 (benchmark), and a Chernoff bound on the sum of the 128 terms with a union bound over every pair of the largest shape keeps every magnitude below 23 (test) and 240 (benchmark) except with probability below 1e-6 (I re-ran r-fwd2's computation). r-fwd's Cauchy-Schwarz bound (36 and 375) is consistent with it and weaker. The README's tolerance at these values is updated to match: about 0.43% (test, X = 23) and 2.9% (benchmark, X = 240).
A library wording issue: SEMANTICS 'Performance-only arguments' versus 'Loops' on num_stages and warp_specialize. The coordinator logged it as L122. The kernel's model omits both, as 'Loops' says.

Wording only, no item digest changed. (1) The test and benchmark line ranges are corrected (see F1). (2) testInst's docstring and README (Proof) now call it a covered instance with the test's smallest N_CTX and HEAD_DIM and its sm_scale, one head (Z = H = 1, which the test does not use: its H is 2 or 48). (3) HeadOk's docstring and README now give one estimate, below 23 (test) and 240 (benchmark) except with probability below 1e-6, with the Chernoff and union-bound argument (see F2).

A library wording issue: SEMANTICS 'Float + and -' does not say whether a tl.maximum, tl.minimum or tl.where result carrying a product's value counts as a product. The coordinator logged it as L123. The model follows the reading that such a result is not a product (lines 84 and 241 as IEEE tl.sub and tl.add).
